FL-014.label: Every memory records the folder the agent stood in when it was made.
FL-014.walk: `/remember` while the agent stands in a folder; the card shows that folder as WHERE.
FL-014.observed: Created the silver-ruler fact while standing in the disposable check subfolder. The card shows that exact absolute WHERE and project path.

FL-017.label: Every prompt is intercepted and relevant memories are added to the context before the model runs.
FL-017.walk: Send a prompt in a thread with memories; the Injection Console shows the memories added before the model ran.
FL-017.observed: The real first prompt paused before model execution with the amber-prism memory and its score. Continue then allowed the model turn; the recorded injection precedes its reply.

FL-018.label: A hard pause on a thread's first prompt where the user scans and removes injected memories before the model starts; afterwards removal is ad hoc with no pause.
FL-018.walk: New thread, first prompt; the gate opens with the memories and waits; the second prompt does not pause.
FL-018.observed: A new fixture thread paused at its first memory gate; after Continue the next real OpenRouter turn ran without another gate. Subsequent trace and transcript show the retained context.

FL-019.label: One-tap removal of an injected memory, with near-miss memories just below the cutoff shown so they can be added back.
FL-019.walk: At the gate, tap × on one memory and add one near-miss back; the count line updates.
FL-019.observed: Count line changed to 1 removed / 1 added after a near-miss veto and another near-miss add. Default removal of an injected real memory was also walked separately. This is partial: the exact combined injected-remove plus near-add sequence was not captured in one gate.

FL-020.label: A one-tap removal at the gate means 'not relevant' by default.
FL-020.walk: Tap × on a gate row; the removal is recorded as 'not relevant'.
FL-020.observed: Tapped the injected amber-prism row's default remove control. The resulting real memory history records inject/commit:removed:not_relevant at r6; no wrong/never modifier was selected.

FL-022.label: After the first prompt the user can still see and remove injected memories mid-thread, ad hoc, without being prompted.
FL-022.walk: Mid-thread, remove a memory from the panel; the next turn omits it.
FL-022.observed: Popped the delivery-day memory off through the Nebula trace, then sent the next prompt. trace-events.csv records mid_thread_removed and its absence from the next prepare; added north-gate memory remained kept.

FL-031.label: The gate as a visualization-plus-input module showing each memory's injection score.
FL-031.walk: The gate overlay shows each memory's injection score and takes removals.
FL-031.observed: Real gate displayed the injection total and component bars; default removal was accepted before Continue. The amber-prism revision records not_relevant feedback.

FL-033.label: Constitution: A near-miss 'never show this' veto (Aug 21 leak-fix packet).
FL-033.walk: Press and hold × on a near-miss; it never reappears in that thread's near-misses.
FL-033.observed: PASS: real 911 ms pointer hold opened the menu before mouse-up. Fixed its missing CSS positioning context; clicked Never show this, continued a real GPT-4.1 mini turn, sent a second prompt. SQL records removed:never on first injection and no vetoed ID in the next injection; long-press-fixed-held.jpg, long-press-veto.jpg, injection-events.txt.

FL-070.label: Image input: paste an image and the agent reviews it.
FL-070.walk: Paste an image; the agent reviews it.
FL-070.observed: Pasted an actual JPEG of the fictional gate into a real GPT-4.1 mini thread. The agent identified Orchard delivery gate and Never show this. An earlier MIME-mismatched paste was a verification mistake and was corrected.

FL-102.label: The Deck: a flashcard stack of terminals, cards colored to match their agents, only one card on top at a time (that project's agent's last response) to interact with, the next card popping up once you respond, ordered purely by which finished first.
FL-102.walk: Answer the top card; it pops and the next card, the earliest to finish, comes up in its agent's color.
FL-102.observed: Two waiting fixture conversations were present. Fired the oldest card and saw it leave the deck, exposing the next waiting card with its thread coloring and Undo/Next up controls.

FL-104.label: A draft response to the final synthesis that you tweak and fire, after which the stack switches to the agent that has waited longest for your attention.
FL-104.walk: Tweak the draft on the top card and fire it; the stack moves to the agent that has waited longest.
FL-104.observed: Edited the top draft to Reply only reviewed, pressed Enter, and observed the waiting count fall from two to one and the next waiting agent become current.

FL-105.label: An Ableton-like rack: the shipped layout is only version one of the default opinion, and people can easily roll and add their own plugins and visualizers to the views from the ground up.
FL-105.walk: Add a self-authored plugin to the rack; it appears among the modules and works.
FL-105.observed: Imported the self-authored M3MU Calibration plugin manifest using the Library. Its isolated iframe rendered the fictional calibration text among the normal modules.

FL-110.label: Global or current on every module; current modules switch together with the work.
FL-110.walk: Set two modules to current and select a different project; both switch together while a global one stays.
FL-110.observed: Created and selected a thread in the disposable check subfolder. Conversation and Memory followed that thread/project together; Spend retained its Global scope.

FL-111.label: One standard module template that can be dragged and grown or shrunk as much as you want, with a dialogue box for its internal settings, on a very large canvas you can pan and zoom while modules stay the same size.
FL-111.walk: Grow a module far past its starting size, open its settings dialogue, then zoom the canvas out; the module grew without a cap and keeps its size as the canvas zooms.
FL-111.observed: Dragged the fixture module corner from approximately (633,746) to (1050,852), opened settings, and zoomed the stage out. Its enlarged footprint remained. This used the desktop viewport where resize handles are available.

FL-112.label: Tabs as layers of the same stage; Injection and Graph as ordinary modules; a gear beside the title for rarely changed options.
FL-112.walk: Add a tab, place the Injection module on it, and open the gear beside the title; the tab is a layer of the same stage and the gear holds the rarely changed options.
FL-112.observed: Added Layer 1, placed Injection Console there, and opened its title gear. The console is another placement on the same stage rather than a separate application.

FL-113.label: A finer, near-continuous background grid, more descriptive well-formatted hover tips, an easy way to create tabs, a much smaller archive button, a model device that is obviously clickable.
FL-113.walk: Hover a control on the stage; a well-formatted descriptive tip appears, the grid behind is near-continuous, a tab can be created easily, the archive button is small, and the model device looks clickable.
FL-113.observed: Observed focus descriptions, stage grid, layer creation, compact archive control and clickable model device. The literal hover plus complete grouped visual criteria were not all walked; no full PASS is claimed.

FL-115.label: Attunement to a specific stack beyond global and current.
FL-115.walk: Set a module to a specific stack; it shows it is aligned to that stack, not global or current.
